prerequisites: It is highly recommended that students have acquired the competencies corresponding to the subjects of previous semesters, especially those related to the subject Business (Course: Organization and Business Management).

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for organization and planning in the field of business and other institutions and organizations.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
That students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in competence G01.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Applied knowledge of logistics systems and production management.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to adapt to new situations.
Ability to communicate with non-experts in the field.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Ability for autonomous and deep learning.
Ability to manage information in solving problematic situations.
Ability for critical reasoning.
Assertive behavior.
Interpersonal relationship skills.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Ability to plan the creation and operation of a company.
Calculate and interpret an aggregate production plan.
Differentiate different aggregate planning strategies.
Calculate and interpret a master production plan.
Solve different lot-sizing techniques.
Calculate and interpret a materials plan.
Calculate and interpret different operation scheduling activities.
Differentiate tactical activities in the production subsystem.
Define the different types of objectives and strategies that can be formulated in the production subsystem.
Distinguish the areas of the company.
Answer fundamental questions in inventory planning through inventory models.
Describe the functions and types of inventories.

syllabus_topics: Theme 1. Introduction to production planning and control
Other aspects of interest in inventory planning and control
Stages in the aggregate planning process
Stages in obtaining the master production schedule
Basic scheme of the original MRP
Theme 6. Very short-term planning and control
teaching_methods: Theory sessions (exposing theoretical foundations, complemented with bibliographic sources)
Practical classes (problem solving, individual work, group work)
Non-contact formative activities (autonomous study, bibliography search, resource search for activities)
assessment_rules: The final theoretical exam may consist of multiple-choice questions (correct answers score 1, incorrect answers subtract 0.33 points, unanswered questions score 0), short questions, or development questions. The final practical exams consist of exercises for which valid answers are those obtained correctly, exactly, and reasonably. Test-type quizzes follow the same scoring rules as multiple-choice questions in the theoretical exam. The group activity can be theoretical and/or practical.
